terra.problem: The ironing joke makes God's garment the target of the humor.
The parking-spot joke targets God and the picture of His chariot.
The claim that the valleys were underwater long before the water got to them is contradictory and adds a timeline the text does not give.
The salad bar introduces a non-cookie food in a joke.
“Different bird” doesn't fit the contrast: livestock are not birds.
The landscaper joke makes God's planting the target of the humor.
The passage describes places for creatures but does not say none has to compete for space.
The passage says the mountains and cliffs are places for these animals; it does not say the wild places belong to them.
The passage does not rule out lions being in pastures. It says they lie down in their dens.
The passage does not say the lions' dens cannot be in valleys.
“Wrong verse” uses “wrong” about the baker's answer.
The psalm does not describe Leviathan as huge.
“Plain words are the kindest way to say it” comments on how Papa tells the passage.
Being silenced is not the opposite of being created, and the verse does not say whether there is quiet.
The joke compares Papa touching a hot pan with God touching the mountains, casting Papa in God's role.
The writer hopes his meditation will be pleasing; he does not say that it is pleasing.
